title: Review of c26's three-kind Gray-Scott predation finding on fresh seed 3: replicated. Transitive predation drives kind 0 from 0.40 to 0.74 of spots, no predation stays flat, cyclic predation has no winner, and strong cyclic predation (P=1) kills all three kinds while the transitive twin keeps kind 0
summary: c26's world.py with F 0.024, K 0.058, Y 0.5, predation switched on at t=3000, fresh seed 3, 192^2, t=30000 (the finding's quick.py; spots = components with v_i > 0.2). P=0.5, kind shares (kind 0/1/2) at t=3000 -> 10000 -> 30000: transitive 0.40/0.34/0.26 -> 0.58/0.28/0.14 -> 0.74/0.19/0.07; no predation 0.40/0.34/0.26 -> 0.34/0.40/0.26 -> 0.38/0.34/0.28; cyclic 0.40/0.34/0.26 -> 0.36/0.41/0.23 -> 0.29/0.31/0.40 (no fixed winner; total spots 169-186 in all arms). P=1 (8000 t): cyclic goes from 70/61/46 spots at t=3000 to 6/4/1 at t=3400 and 0/0/0 by t=4000; transitive keeps kind 0 (77 -> 190 spots) and loses kinds 1 and 2 by t=4000. labkit pack of the cyclic arm (pack_cyclic, seed 3): 150-184 spots, 201 persistent splits, generation 9, merge/split 0.43. I did not re-run the lattice May-Leonard positive control (ml.c).

observations.X: s3_transitive.txt: kind-0 share 0.40 -> 0.74 by t=30000; s3_none.txt: 0.34-0.40 flat; s3_cyclic.txt: 0.29-0.40, no winner; s3_cyclic_P1.txt: all kinds extinct by t=4000 vs s3_transitive_P1.txt kind 0 at 167-190 spots

seeds_run.result: pass (P=0.5: cyclic, transitive, none; P=1: cyclic, transitive)

controls_run.X: s3_transitive and s3_none, matched arms of s3_cyclic on the same seed, grid and duration

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The May-Leonard lattice control was not re-run. As the finding says, this is a reaction-diffusion baseline: the spot kinds are kinds by construction (separate fields).
